answer: A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own signal path. Since the saffron verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the pigment audit keeps every accepted path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 17 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. That is 36 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
